anomalies.observed: The netlist shows all six 0 Ω jumpers connected: R4 bridges the two servo signal pins, R9 connects the shared servo signal to the MAX3485 A line (/NET0010), and R7/R20/R8/R22 connect the PWM selection nets /NET0019 and /NET0027 to M5Stack bus pins 19/21 and 20/22. Through R16/R4/R15/R9, the PWM GPIO nets and the MAX3485 serial bus are therefore bridged together.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that PWM and serial servo modes are mutually exclusive and are selected by populating different 0 Ω jumpers. In PWM mode, the serial bridge jumpers should be open and only the appropriate PWM selection jumper for the Core variant should be populated. In serial mode, the serial bridge jumpers may be populated, but the PWM selection jumpers should not be populated.

evidence.quote: It supports two mutually-exclusive servo interface modes, selected at assembly time by populating different 0 Ω jumper resistors
PWM mode (populate R3/R4, and the appropriate R9–R12 pair for the Core variant; leave R13/R14 open)
Serial mode (populate R13/R14, per the explicit schematic annotation "Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo")

anomalies.impact: The board cannot cleanly select PWM or serial servo mode. The PWM GPIO nets are tied together and to the MAX3485 A bus through low-resistance paths, which can cause signal contention, incorrect servo control, loading of the serial bus by unused GPIOs, and possible damage if M5Stack GPIOs are driven while the serial transceiver is also driving the same node.

parsed.summary: The passive values and power/UART/battery topology otherwise match the specification, but the netlist connects both the serial-mode bridge jumpers and all PWM selection jumpers, violating the intended mutually-exclusive PWM/serial jumper configuration and bridging the PWM GPIO nets with the MAX3485 serial bus.
